newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end lower for fourth day.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end lower for fourth day.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower in thin trading for the fourth consecutive day on Thursday, traders said, recovering after an initial dive at news of the killing of seven Israel schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.13 percent, or 2.83 points, to 246.64 on low all-share turnover of 108 million shekels against 97 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.05 percent lower at 253.24.

"The session opened with heavy supply. After the news broke about the killing in Jordan, the market fell by almost two percent only to recover towards the end of the day," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.
A Jordanian soldier on Thursday shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls and wounded six while the children were on a field trip to the Israeli-Jordanian border.
"Paradoxically, this event might lead to an improvement in peace talks, easing the pressure on Israel," Scharia added.
The attack came amid a crisis in peacemaking over Israeli plans to build a Jewish neighborhood in Arab East Jerusalem.

"The market is very quiet and the it is looking for a new saturation point. The market made a big move, then came a correction, and now it's reaching an equilibrium," said Shahar Gazit at Batucha Securities and Investments.
Scharia added that investors were also waiting for the release on Friday of the February consumer price index. Analysts predict the CPI will show a 1.1-1.2 percent rise over January.
The most active share was Teva Pharmaceutical Industries which fell 3.0 percent to 20,220 agorot on volume of 5 million shekels.
Elite Industries, the second most active share, rose 3.25 percent to 8,246 agorot on turnover of 4.7 million shekels.

Elite said on Thursday that 1996 net profit rose to 18.1 million shekels from net loss of 6.8 million in 1995. It also said that the Federman group put in motion a mechanism to dissolve shared control of the company with Gideon Holdings.
"If Strauss takes over its good news for the company and the price will rise sharply. Investors want to see Federman leave the company," one trader said.
Bank Leumi, gained 0.25 to 539 on turnover of 4.3 million shekels.
